MERIDIAN

MERIDIAN is an R Shiny application for analysing multi-environment crop trials. It brings data validation, exploratory plots, design-aware models, genotype stability, environmental covariates and report export into one interface.

The name stands for Multi-Environment Research Integration: Data Intelligence and Agronomic Networks.

Installation

Install from GitHub and launch the application:

install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("SalvaOsuna/MERIDIAN")

MERIDIAN::run_app()

R 4.3.0 or later is required. Windows users need Rtools matching their R release; macOS users need Apple’s Command Line Tools. Linux users need a compiler and development libraries. See the installation guide for instructions for each system and optional PDF export requirements.

Getting started

Choose Load Example Data in the welcome dialog to explore a simulated trial with 20 genotypes, five environments, three replicates and four traits. The example includes environmental covariates and works without internet access.

You can also inspect those data directly in R:

trial <- read.csv(system.file(
  "extdata", "example_phenotypic.csv", package = "MERIDIAN"
))

dim(trial)
#> [1] 300  10

aggregate(GrainYield ~ Environment, data = trial, FUN = mean)
#>   Environment GrainYield
#> 1        ENV1   4.821864
#> 2        ENV2   4.041333
#> 3        ENV3   4.520847
#> 4        ENV4   5.225833
#> 5        ENV5   3.888833

These are raw descriptive means. Adjusted genotype means and formal inference require the experimental-design settings in the app. The getting-started guide explains data preparation and your first analysis.

Analysis workflow

Module Main tasks
Overview Import CSV or Excel; map genotype, environment, replicate, block and trait columns; validate records.
Traits Inspect distributions, missing values, outliers, G×E means and environment correlations.
ANOVA Fit design-adjusted ANOVA and mixed models; inspect variance components, Cullis generalized heritability, BLUEs and BLUPs.
Stability Explore AMMI, GGE, Eberhart–Russell, Wricke and Shukla statistics.
Adaptation Inspect observed winners, reaction norms, environmental PCA and covariate associations.
Field Map Fit single-environment SpATS models and inspect spatial trends and adjusted means.
Reports Register selected results, compose figures and export tables, plots and HTML/PDF reports.

Analyses use the mapped design and the selected trait. Changing data or model settings invalidates affected results. Outputs sent to Reports are frozen snapshots, so later recalculation cannot silently change an exported result.

See the analysis and interpretation guide for the full workflow, model assumptions and an environmental-index example.

Examples in R

The app is the main entry point. A small set of exported helpers can also be used in scripts. For example, display correlations between environments:

MERIDIAN::plot_env_correlation(
  trial,
  gen_col = "Genotype",
  env_col = "Environment",
  trait = "GrainYield",
  method = "pearson"
)

The function reference documents the launcher, environment-correlation plot, date parsing, weather retrieval and agroclimatic indices. Weather retrieval requires internet access; the examples in the guides use bundled or explicitly simulated data.

Exporting results

Send a plot or table from an analysis module to Reports. From there you can download CSV/Excel tables, PNG/PDF/SVG/TIFF figures, composed multi-panel figures or a complete HTML/PDF report. HTML reports need Pandoc. PDF reports additionally need pagedown and Chrome, Chromium or Edge.

Statistical scope

MERIDIAN supports RCBD, incomplete-block and augmented designs when the supplied data identify the required effects. Missing observations are handled separately for each trait and analysis. The mixed model currently assumes independent G×E effects and homogeneous residual variance. Winner groups are exploratory; across-environment averages of separate spatial fits are descriptive summaries.

Review design diagnostics, missing-cell processing and uncertainty before using results for selection. Further details are in the analysis guide.

Help and development

Report reproducible problems or request improvements in the GitHub issue tracker. Source code, tests and development instructions are available in the repository.
